patients.label: 85-year-old man with marginal zone lymphoma on ibrutinib and rituximab who developed pulmonary tuberculosis

identity_evidence.quote: An 85‐year‐old man from Ivory Coast (West Africa)

attribution_limitations: The authors raise, without establishing, a possible impact of ibrutinib treatment on the onset or reactivation of tuberculosis in subjects at risk; whether this patient had reactivation of latent infection or new infection, and any causal role of ibrutinib or rituximab, is not stated for him. No cause is inferred.

The CT time "after 6 months of therapy" follows the sentence on ibrutinib plus rituximab; the sentence does not itself name the drugs, so the therapy is read as that combination. The sentence on anti-tuberculous treatment gives its durations but no start date or order relative to the CT.

claims.text: An 85-year-old man from Ivory Coast who frequently traveled to Africa had been followed since 1997 for marginal zone lymphoma with an immunoglobulin M component and translocation (11;18). He had hypertension, Guillain-Barre syndrome and no history of HIV. He received chloraminophene (1997 to 2001) for anemia and medullary involvement, rituximab-cyclophosphamide (2008) after an intestinal recurrence, rituximab-bendamustine (2011) for a gastric relapse, and in 2018 ibrutinib 420 mg orally per day with monthly rituximab for a large mesenteric recurrence.

Neutrophils were 1.15 G/L, lymphocytes 1.1 G/L, with mild hypogammaglobulinemia at 6 g/L.
